explanations.1: These lines define ANSI color codes that will be used later to colorize terminal output—34 is blue, 36 is cyan, and 33 is yellow.
explanations.8: This sets PHP_VERSION to 8.1 if it hasn't already been defined elsewhere (like in a .env file), using the $(or ...) function to provide a fallback.
explanations.10: This constructs the full Docker image name by inserting the PHP version number into the template string.
explanations.13: These are the standard Docker flags: -it keeps it interactive, --rm cleans up after, -v mounts folders so the container can access your code and write temporary files.
explanations.16: This captures your current user and group IDs so files created inside Docker won't be owned by root, preventing permission headaches later.
explanations.25: The $(eval ...) syntax creates a local variable called COMMAND that holds the phan command string; it's a Makefile-specific way to define variables inside a target.
explanations.26: The \e[1;${COLOR_YELLOW}m...\e[0m is ANSI escape code syntax that colors the output yellow; \e[0m at the end resets the color back to normal.
explanations.37: Similar to line 25, this creates a local COMMAND variable with the php-cs-fixer command, but it will be appended with --dry-run later to preview changes without applying them.
